svg.title: init repairs its own GitLab connection when something breaks it — init re-creates a revoked automation token end to end
svg.text: init repairs its own GitLab connection when something
Scenario: init re-creates a revoked automation token end to end

g.text: Given a project the framework has already set up with its automation
token
A fresh project after its first `task devsecops:init`: the access-tokens page shows the
automation token init created. Off-camera: the lambda user, the fresh project, the setup
that ran init once. Dates that change every run are masked.
When the developer revokes the automation token behind the framework's
back
The token is revoked from outside the framework (as if someone deleted it in GitLab): the
access-tokens page no longer lists the automation token. The test also checks through the
API that no automation token is active anymore.
And the developer runs the framework's init again
A single `task devsecops:init` re-run: the finishing message shows it noticed the token was
missing and created a new one. The test also checks the command succeeded.
Then init has created a brand-new automation token
The access-tokens page shows the automation token again. The test also checks through the
API that exactly one is active and it is not the same token as before.
And init has updated the CI/CD variable to match the new token
The CI/CD variables page shows the variable again, now pointing at the new token. The test
also checks through the API that the variable exists and has a value.
And the healed token clones the repository over HTTPS
The healed token signs in to GitLab and lists the repository over HTTPS (the secret and
commit IDs are masked). The test also does a full clone with both the automation token and
the Renovate token, to prove they both actually work.
When the developer runs init a second time
A second `task devsecops:init` on the already-healed project: the finishing message reports
the token is already in place, nothing to recreate. The test also checks the command
succeeded.
Then the second run leaves the healed token untouched
The access-tokens page has not changed: still one automation token. The test also checks
through the API that it is the exact same token as before — init does not quietly replace it
on every run.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 8 steps · 8 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
